Re: Formal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Casey Kimura
Member ID: W414616133
Reference Number: POC-3A74C3E137-54728
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-13
Requested Service: Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
Treating Surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Grievance and Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), as set out in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-13, reference number POC-3A74C3E137-54728. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day window stated in that notice (deadline 2027-02-09).

**Stated reason for denial**
The notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." The notice further states that the determination was made "under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria," without naming or quoting that policy in the letter itself.

**Identification of the applicable clinical criteria**
Based on my own research, Anthem's medical-necessity review for joint replacement procedures, including CPT 27130, in Missouri has been transitioned to Carelon Medical Benefits Management's Musculoskeletal Program. The document that appears to govern this procedure is the Carelon "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery," Hip Arthroplasty section, Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, "Status: Revised Effective Date: 11/15/2025," "Last Review Date: 04/21/2025." I was able to retrieve the following language directly from that document's public listing:

- "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)"
- "Physical exam consistent with symptomatic hip arthritis (e.g., pain with passive motion of the hip, antalgic gait, limited motion) unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, diffuse modified Outerbridge grade 4, or Tonnis grade 3"
- "Functional limitation secondary to hip pathology which interferes with the ability to perform age-appropriate daily activities"
- "Primary total hip arthroplasty or conversion of a previous intra-articular or implant hip surgery to a hip arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:" including "Joint damage or destruction due to osteoarthritis, inflammatory disease, or other chronic condition when ALL of the following requirements have been met:"

I was not able to retrieve the complete Hip Arthroplasty section of this document in full (the imaging-grading detail, the complete contraindications list, and the exact full text of every sub-bullet were not accessible to me), so I am not quoting or characterizing any language beyond what is shown above. If this is not in fact the correct or complete criteria document that was applied to my request, I am formally requesting, under my right to the specific rule, guideline, or protocol relied upon in this denial, that Anthem provide me with a copy of the exact criteria document, section, and edition applied to reference number POC-3A74C3E137-54728, along with its title, policy/document number, and effective date.

**Response to the stated denial reason, mapped to the clinical record**

The clinical record submitted with the prior authorization request in fact documents an extensive and appropriately supervised trial of conservative treatment that meets or exceeds the "at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management" standard quoted above:

1. Duration and severity of symptoms: I have had 12 months of progressive hip pain that is unrelieved by rest.
2. Physical therapy: I completed 18 visits of supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait training over a 14-week course, from 2026-03-13 through 2026-06-19, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Fourteen weeks of supervised, documented therapy exceeds the 12-week conservative-management benchmark quoted above.
3. Medication trial: I was treated with NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief of symptoms.
4. Injection therapy: I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-06, which produced only 2 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.

Taken together, these records show a supervised, multi-modality conservative treatment trial — physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and image-guided injection — that was of adequate duration and failed to relieve my symptoms. I am asking the plan to identify specifically what additional conservative treatment, of what type and duration, it believes is missing from this record, since the record as submitted appears to satisfy the conservative-treatment element quoted above.

**Additional clinical findings supporting medical necessity**

- Imaging: A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph obtained 2026-07-19 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophyte formation. [If a formal Kellgren-Lawrence, Tönnis, or Outerbridge grade was assigned by the radiologist or Dr. Duval, please add that grade here, as the guideline language I was able to retrieve refers to these specific grading systems.]
- Physical examination: Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected hip and range of motion limited by pain, which are consistent with the "physical exam consistent with symptomatic hip arthritis" language quoted above.
- Functional limitation: I currently ambulate with a cane, am limited to walking one block, and cannot put on my shoes unassisted. This directly reflects the "functional limitation secondary to hip pathology which interferes with the ability to perform age-appropriate daily activities" criterion quoted above.
- No disqualifying factors are present: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

**Requested action**

Based on the above, I ask that Anthem:
1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27130 (total hip replacement), to be performed by Dr. Duval.
2. If any additional documentation is needed, please contact Dr. Duval's office at [surgeon's office phone/fax] or me directly, and specify exactly what documentation is missing.
3. If the plan intends to uphold the denial, please arrange a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Duval and the reviewing physician before issuing a final decision, and provide the complete text of the specific medical policy or clinical guideline, including title, document/policy number, section, and effective date, that was applied to this request.
4. Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide the applicable timeframe for a decision under the plan's internal appeal procedures, as well as information on my right to an independent external review if this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor.

Enclosed with this letter are copies of: the physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-13 to 2026-06-19), documentation of the 6-month NSAID trial, the corticosteroid injection record dated 2026-04-06, the weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph report dated 2026-07-19, and Dr. Duval's clinical notes documenting exam findings and functional limitations. [List/attach any additional records not already described above.]

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone number, and email listed above, with a copy to Dr. Duval's office at [surgeon's office address/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Casey Kimura
